questions.question: A program is:

options.C: A collection of instructions normally stored in secondary storage

questions.explanation: A program is a collection of instructions normally stored in secondary storage.

questions.question: A process is:
questions.explanation: A process is a program in execution.

questions.question: A program is a:
questions.explanation: A program is a passive entity because it just sits on disk.

questions.question: A process is an:
questions.explanation: A process is an active entity because it is executing.

questions.question: A Process Control Block (PCB) belongs to a:
questions.explanation: A PCB is created and kept by the OS for each process.

questions.question: The five states of a process are:
questions.explanation: The five process states are New, Ready, Running, Waiting and Terminated.

questions.question: A process that is waiting for the CPU is in the:
questions.explanation: A process waiting for the CPU is in the Ready state.

questions.question: A process whose instructions are being executed by the CPU is in the:
questions.explanation: A process being executed by the CPU is in the Running state.

questions.question: A process waiting for an I/O operation to complete is in the:
questions.explanation: A process waiting for I/O is in the Blocked/Waiting state.

questions.question: A process that has finished execution is in the:
questions.explanation: A process that has finished execution is in the Terminated state.

questions.question: The two states of the Two-State model are:
questions.explanation: The Two-State model has only Running and Not Running.

questions.question: The Seven-State model adds which two states to the five-state model?
questions.explanation: The Seven-State model adds Suspend Ready and Suspend Blocked.

questions.question: The transition Running → Ready is called:
questions.explanation: Running → Ready, when the process is removed from the CPU, is preemption.

questions.question: The long-term scheduler is also called the:
questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler is also called the job scheduler.

questions.question: The short-term scheduler is also called the:
questions.explanation: The short-term scheduler is also called the CPU scheduler.

questions.question: The medium-term scheduler mainly handles:
questions.explanation: The medium-term scheduler handles swapping processes out of and into memory.

questions.question: The degree of multiprogramming is the:

options.A: Number of processes in the system for execution at a time

questions.explanation: The degree of multiprogramming is the number of processes in the system for execution at a time.

questions.question: A process that spends most of its time doing calculations is:
questions.explanation: A CPU-bound process spends most of its time doing calculations.

questions.question: A process that spends much time waiting for I/O is:
questions.explanation: An I/O-bound process spends much of its time waiting for I/O.

questions.question: IPC stands for:
questions.explanation: IPC stands for Inter-Process Communication.

questions.question: The two major IPC approaches are:
questions.explanation: The two major IPC approaches are shared memory and message passing.

questions.question: Message passing commonly uses:
questions.explanation: Message passing commonly uses pipes, message queues and sockets.

questions.question: Shared memory access is controlled using:
questions.explanation: Shared memory access is controlled with semaphores, mutexes and locks.

questions.question: A race condition occurs when the final result depends on the:

options.D: Order in which processes access shared data

questions.explanation: A race condition occurs when the result depends on the order in which processes access shared data.

questions.question: Deadlock means that processes:

options.A: Wait indefinitely for resources held by one another

questions.explanation: Deadlock means processes wait indefinitely for resources held by one another.

questions.question: Starvation means a process:

options.B: Keeps waiting for resources or a chance to execute

questions.explanation: Starvation means a process keeps waiting for resources or a chance to execute.

questions.question: How many philosophers are in the Dining Philosophers problem?
questions.explanation: The Dining Philosophers problem has five philosophers.

questions.question: In the Producer–Consumer problem, the processes share a:
questions.explanation: Producers and consumers share a buffer.

questions.question: In the Readers–Writers problem, a writer needs:
questions.explanation: A writer needs exclusive access to the shared data.

questions.question: The Sleeping Barber problem has:
questions.explanation: The Sleeping Barber problem has one barber.

questions.question: PID stands for:

options.B: Process Identifier (unique number of a process)

questions.explanation: PID stands for Process Identifier, the unique number of a process.

questions.question: The Program Counter (PC) holds the:
questions.explanation: The Program Counter holds the address of the next instruction.

questions.question: The Memory Address Register (MAR) holds a memory:
questions.explanation: The MAR holds a memory address.

questions.question: The Memory Data Register (MDR) holds:

options.B: Data being transferred between CPU and memory

questions.explanation: The MDR holds data being transferred between the CPU and memory.

questions.question: The Instruction Register (IR) holds the:
questions.explanation: The IR holds the current fetched instruction.

questions.question: The Stack Pointer (SP) points to the:
questions.explanation: The Stack Pointer points to the current top of the stack.

questions.question: The fastest storage among the following is:
questions.explanation: CPU registers are the fastest storage of the options given.

questions.question: The process table contains:
questions.explanation: The process table has one entry for each process.

questions.question: Context switching means:

options.C: Saving the state of one process and loading the saved state of another

questions.explanation: Context switching saves the state of one process and loads the saved state of another.

questions.question: Context-switch overhead is the:
questions.explanation: Context-switch overhead is the time spent on switching-related work.

questions.question: A mode switch changes the:

options.B: CPU privilege or execution mode, such as user to kernel

questions.explanation: A mode switch changes the CPU privilege or execution mode, such as user to kernel.

questions.question: The scheduler:

options.B: Hands over the CPU physically only

questions.explanation: The scheduler selects which process should run.

questions.question: The dispatcher:

options.C: Gives CPU control to the process selected by the scheduler

questions.explanation: The dispatcher gives CPU control to the process selected by the scheduler.

questions.question: CPU utilisation is the:

options.D: Percentage of time the CPU is busy doing useful work

questions.explanation: CPU utilisation is the percentage of time the CPU is busy doing useful work.

questions.question: Throughput is the:

options.A: Number of processes completed per unit time

questions.explanation: Throughput is the number of processes completed per unit time.

questions.question: Turnaround time is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Turnaround time = completion time − arrival time.

questions.question: Waiting time is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Waiting time = turnaround time − burst time.

questions.question: Response time is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Response time = first CPU time − arrival time.

questions.question: FCFS is a:
questions.explanation: FCFS is a non-preemptive scheduling algorithm.

questions.question: Round Robin is a:
questions.explanation: Round Robin is a preemptive algorithm because of its time slice.

questions.question: Why does a program have no PCB?

options.B: The OS creates the PCB only when the program is executed as a process

questions.explanation: The OS creates a PCB only when a program is executed as a process, so a program has none.

questions.question: Which example shows that one program can have multiple processes?

options.D: A web browser using different processes for different tabs

questions.explanation: A web browser using separate processes for tabs shows one program with multiple processes.

questions.question: Which resources are needed by a process?

options.A: CPU time, memory, I/O resources and files

questions.explanation: A process needs CPU time, memory, I/O resources and files.

questions.question: The transition when a process's time slice expires is:
questions.explanation: When the time slice expires, the process moves from Running to Ready.

questions.question: When an awaited I/O operation completes, the process moves from:
questions.explanation: When the awaited I/O completes, the process moves from Blocked to Ready.

questions.question: Which state normally occurs only once in a process's lifetime?
questions.explanation: The New state occurs only once, when the process is created.

questions.question: A process in the Suspend Ready state is:

options.C: Ready to execute but temporarily moved out of main memory

questions.explanation: Suspend Ready means ready to execute but temporarily moved out of main memory.

questions.question: A process in the Suspend Blocked state is:

options.A: Waiting for an event and also swapped out of main memory

questions.explanation: Suspend Blocked means waiting for an event and also swapped out of main memory.

questions.question: Which scheduler controls the degree of multiprogramming?
questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler controls the degree of multiprogramming.

questions.question: Which scheduler executes most frequently?
questions.explanation: The short-term scheduler runs most frequently, at every CPU allocation.

questions.question: What does preemptive execution mean?

options.A: The OS can forcibly remove a running process from the CPU
options.B: A process can never be interrupted
options.D: A process never uses the CPU

questions.explanation: Preemptive execution means the OS can forcibly remove a running process from the CPU.

questions.question: On a single-processor system, the number of processes in the Running state at one instant is:
questions.explanation: A single-processor system has exactly one process in the Running state at an instant.

questions.question: Shared memory IPC is generally fast because:

options.B: Processes access memory directly after it is set up

questions.explanation: After setup, processes access shared memory directly, which makes it fast.

questions.question: Synchronization is needed in shared memory because:

options.A: Simultaneous access to the same data can cause inconsistent results

questions.explanation: Simultaneous access to the same data can cause inconsistent results, so synchronization is needed.

questions.question: A disadvantage of message passing is:

options.C: It works only on one process
options.D: It may involve more overhead such as copying and kernel involvement

questions.explanation: Message passing may involve more overhead such as copying and kernel involvement.

questions.question: In the Dining Philosophers problem, if every philosopher picks up one fork and waits for the other, the result is:
questions.explanation: If every philosopher holds one fork and waits for the other, the result is deadlock.

questions.question: In the Producer–Consumer problem, the producer must wait when the buffer is:
questions.explanation: The producer must wait when the buffer is full.

questions.question: In the Producer–Consumer problem, the consumer must wait when the buffer is:
questions.explanation: The consumer must wait when the buffer is empty.

questions.question: In the Readers–Writers problem:

options.D: Multiple readers can generally read at the same time

questions.explanation: In Readers–Writers, multiple readers can generally read at the same time.

questions.question: In the Sleeping Barber problem, if all waiting chairs are occupied, a new customer:
questions.explanation: If all waiting chairs are occupied, a new customer leaves.

questions.question: The PCB is stored in:
questions.explanation: The PCB is stored in protected kernel memory.

questions.question: The PCB is saved and restored during:
questions.explanation: The PCB is saved and restored during context switching.

questions.question: Which item is NOT stored in a PCB?

options.D: The contents of the user's video file

questions.explanation: A PCB stores process details such as PID, PC and open files, not the contents of user files.

questions.question: The process table is:

options.C: A collection of entries, each holding a process's PCB information

questions.explanation: The process table is a collection of entries, each holding a process's PCB information.

questions.question: The accumulator is used to store:

options.A: Intermediate results of arithmetic and logical operations

questions.explanation: The accumulator stores intermediate results of arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: In 10 − 10 = 0, which flag is set?
questions.explanation: 10 − 10 = 0, so the Zero flag is set.

questions.question: During a memory read, data flows:
questions.explanation: In a memory read, data flows Memory → MDR → CPU.

questions.question: The correct instruction cycle flow is:
questions.explanation: The instruction cycle is PC → fetch → IR → decode → execute.

questions.question: The correct speed order (fastest to slowest) is:
questions.explanation: Fastest to slowest: registers, cache, RAM, secondary storage.

questions.question: Is the PC always incremented by 4 on a 32-bit system?

options.B: No, it depends on the architecture and instruction size

questions.explanation: The PC increment depends on the architecture and instruction size, so it is not always 4.

questions.question: Which event can cause a context switch?

options.D: A timer interrupt in preemptive multitasking

questions.explanation: A timer interrupt in preemptive multitasking can cause a context switch.

questions.question: Does every interrupt cause a context switch?

options.C: No, the OS may handle it and continue the same process

questions.explanation: Not every interrupt causes a context switch, because the OS may handle it and continue the same process.

questions.question: During a context switch from P0 to P1, the OS:

options.A: Saves P0's context in PCB0 and restores P1's context from PCB1

questions.explanation: On a switch from P0 to P1, the OS saves P0's context in PCB0 and restores P1's from PCB1.

questions.question: A system call causes:

options.B: A mode switch, not necessarily a context switch

questions.explanation: A system call causes a mode switch, not necessarily a context switch.

questions.question: Which hardware feature can speed up context switching?
questions.explanation: Multiple register sets can speed up context switching.

questions.question: Too many context switches reduce:

options.D: The CPU time available for useful application work

questions.explanation: Too many context switches reduce the CPU time available for useful application work.

questions.question: How do the scheduler and dispatcher differ?

options.A: The dispatcher selects; the scheduler gives CPU control
options.B: The scheduler selects the process; the dispatcher transfers CPU control to it

questions.explanation: The scheduler selects the process; the dispatcher transfers CPU control to it.

questions.question: How many types of schedulers are described in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes describe three types of schedulers: long-term, short-term and medium-term.

questions.question: Which is a dispatcher function?

options.C: Restoring the selected process's context and transferring control to it

questions.explanation: The dispatcher restores the selected process's context and transfers control to it.

questions.question: The CPU is busy for 80 s in a 100 s interval. CPU utilisation is:
questions.explanation: Utilisation = 80 / 100 = 80%.

questions.question: 20 processes complete in 10 seconds. The throughput is:
questions.explanation: Throughput = 20 / 10 = 2 processes per second.

questions.question: A process arrives at time 2 and completes at time 12. Its turnaround time is:
questions.explanation: Turnaround time = 12 − 2 = 10.

questions.question: Turnaround time is 15 ms and burst time is 8 ms. The waiting time is:
questions.explanation: Waiting time = 15 − 8 = 7 ms.

questions.question: A process arrives at 4 and first gets the CPU at 7. The response time is:
questions.explanation: Response time = 7 − 4 = 3.

questions.question: Which type of system needs quick response?
questions.explanation: Interactive systems need quick response.

questions.question: Which type of system focuses on throughput and turnaround time?
questions.explanation: Batch systems focus on throughput and turnaround time.

questions.question: Real-time systems mainly need:
questions.explanation: Real-time systems need predictable and timely execution.

questions.question: Which of these is a preemptive algorithm?
questions.explanation: SRTF is preemptive, while FCFS, SJF and LJF are non-preemptive.

questions.question: Which of these is a non-preemptive algorithm?
questions.explanation: SJF is non-preemptive, while Round Robin, SRTF and MLFQ are preemptive.

questions.question: A risk in priority scheduling is:
questions.explanation: A risk in priority scheduling is starvation of low-priority processes.

questions.question: Which statement about a program and a process is correct?

options.A: A program is dynamic and a process is static
options.C: A process is dynamic, a program is static, and processes of one program can have different data and states
options.D: A program needs CPU time but a process does not

questions.explanation: A process is dynamic, a program is static, and processes of one program can have different data and states.

questions.question: Which is NOT a feature of a program?

options.A: It has a Process Control Block
options.C: It is stored in secondary storage
options.D: One program can have many processes

questions.explanation: A program does not have a PCB; the PCB belongs to a process.

questions.question: Which is a valid life cycle of a process?

options.D: New → Ready → Running → Blocked → Ready → Running → Terminated

questions.explanation: The valid life cycle is New → Ready → Running → Blocked → Ready → Running → Terminated.

questions.question: Which transition is NOT described in the process-state notes?
questions.explanation: A blocked process goes to Ready first, so Blocked → Running directly is not described.

questions.question: CPU-bound and I/O-bound describe a process's:
questions.explanation: CPU-bound and I/O-bound describe a process's behaviour, not a state.

questions.question: A process in Suspend Ready returns to Ready after it is:
questions.explanation: A Suspend Ready process returns to Ready after it is brought back into main memory.

questions.question: What is the difference between the long-term and medium-term schedulers?

options.A: Long-term swaps processes; medium-term admits new jobs
options.B: Long-term admits new processes; medium-term swaps processes in and out of memory

questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler admits new processes; the medium-term scheduler swaps processes in and out of memory.

questions.question: Which pairing is WRONG?

options.C: Dispatcher – hands control to the selected process

questions.explanation: The short-term scheduler is the CPU scheduler, not the job scheduler.

questions.question: If the degree of multiprogramming becomes too high:
questions.explanation: A very high degree of multiprogramming increases system overhead.

questions.question: Why can shared memory without synchronization give wrong results?

options.C: Simultaneous access can leave data inconsistent

questions.explanation: Simultaneous access can leave shared data inconsistent.

questions.question: Message passing is especially useful when processes are:
questions.explanation: Message passing is especially useful when processes are isolated from one another.

questions.question: Which is NOT an IPC problem listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: Increased disk capacity is not an IPC problem; race condition, deadlock and starvation are.

questions.question: A solution for the Dining Philosophers problem is to:

options.A: Limit how many philosophers try to eat at once or impose a resource ordering
options.C: Let everyone pick up one fork and wait

questions.explanation: Limiting how many philosophers eat at once, or ordering resources, avoids deadlock.

questions.question: A standard solution to the Producer–Consumer problem uses:
questions.explanation: The standard solution uses a mutex and counting semaphores.

questions.question: A common solution for Readers–Writers is to use:
questions.explanation: Readers–Writers is commonly solved with reader–writer locks or semaphores.

questions.question: The Sleeping Barber problem is solved by using:
questions.explanation: The Sleeping Barber problem is solved using semaphores.

questions.question: Which statement about PCB storage is correct?

options.A: The exact place depends on the OS; it is not correct to say every OS stores the whole PCB at the beginning of the kernel stack
options.B: Every OS stores the PCB at the top of user memory
options.C: The PCB is stored in the CPU cache only
options.D: The PCB is stored on the keyboard

questions.explanation: The place where the PCB is stored depends on the OS, so no single location can be claimed for every OS.

questions.question: The program counter is saved in the PCB so that the process can:
questions.explanation: The saved program counter lets the process resume from the correct instruction.

questions.question: The stack pointer in the PCB helps to preserve:

options.B: The function-call context, local variables and return addresses

questions.explanation: The saved stack pointer preserves function-call context, local variables and return addresses.

questions.question: MAR contains 8000 during a read. What does the MDR hold?
questions.explanation: The MDR holds the data read from the address in the MAR (8000).

questions.question: Which register holds the instruction currently being decoded or executed?
questions.explanation: The IR holds the instruction currently being decoded or executed.

questions.question: Which flag indicates an arithmetic overflow?
questions.explanation: The Overflow flag indicates arithmetic overflow.

questions.question: Which items are saved during a context switch?

options.C: PC, CPU registers, stack pointer and processor status

questions.explanation: A context switch saves the PC, CPU registers, stack pointer and processor status.

questions.question: Which is an example of a mode switch?

options.D: User mode changing to kernel mode on a system call

questions.explanation: User mode changing to kernel mode on a system call is a mode switch.

questions.question: Why is context-switch time called pure overhead?

options.B: The CPU does OS work instead of useful application instructions

questions.explanation: Context-switch time is pure overhead because the CPU does OS work instead of useful application instructions.

questions.question: Which factor affects context-switch time?
questions.explanation: Context-switch time depends on processor architecture and hardware support.

questions.question: Which statement about the dispatcher is correct?

options.A: It selects the process using scheduling algorithms
options.C: It acts on the scheduler's selection and does not choose the process
options.D: It admits jobs from the job pool

questions.explanation: The dispatcher acts on the scheduler's selection and does not choose the process.

questions.question: Which is a common mistake mentioned in the notes?

options.B: Believing the PCB has a PID
options.D: Believing the scheduler itself does everything needed to start the selected process

questions.explanation: A common mistake is believing the scheduler alone does everything needed to start the selected process.

questions.question: A process arrives at 0, completes at 20 and has a burst time of 12. Its waiting time is:
questions.explanation: Turnaround = 20 − 0 = 20, so waiting = 20 − 12 = 8.

questions.question: A process arrives at 3, completes at 15 and has a burst time of 7. Its waiting time is:
questions.explanation: Turnaround = 15 − 3 = 12, so waiting = 12 − 7 = 5.

questions.question: Response time differs from turnaround time because a process may:

options.C: Respond early and continue running afterwards

questions.explanation: Response time differs from turnaround time because a process may respond early and continue running afterwards.

questions.question: Waiting time does NOT include the process's:
questions.explanation: Waiting time does not include execution time.

questions.question: The CPU is busy for 45 s in a 60 s interval. Utilisation is:
questions.explanation: Utilisation = 45 / 60 = 75%.

questions.question: 30 processes complete in 6 seconds. Throughput is:
questions.explanation: Throughput = 30 / 6 = 5 per second.

questions.question: A process arrives at 5 and first gets the CPU at 9. The response time is:
questions.explanation: Response time = 9 − 5 = 4.

questions.question: Throughput depends on the workload because:

options.A: Short and long processes need different amounts of CPU time

questions.explanation: Throughput depends on the workload because short and long processes need different CPU time.

questions.question: Predictability as a criterion means:

options.D: The algorithm gives consistent performance for similar workloads

questions.explanation: Predictability means consistent performance for similar workloads.

questions.question: Which algorithm gives each process a fixed time slice?
questions.explanation: Round Robin gives each process a fixed time slice.

questions.question: SJF selects the process with:
questions.explanation: SJF selects the process with the shortest CPU burst.

questions.question: Which list contains only non-preemptive algorithms?
questions.explanation: FCFS, SJF and LJF are all non-preemptive.

questions.question: Which list contains only preemptive algorithms?
questions.explanation: RR, SRTF and preemptive priority are all preemptive.

questions.question: Multilevel Feedback Queue scheduling is classified as:
questions.explanation: Multilevel Feedback Queue scheduling is preemptive.

questions.question: In priority scheduling, low-priority processes may suffer:
questions.explanation: In priority scheduling, low-priority processes may suffer starvation.

questions.question: Which factors affect the choice of a scheduling algorithm?

options.C: Number of processes, CPU burst time, urgency and system requirements

questions.explanation: The choice depends on the number of processes, CPU burst time, urgency and system requirements.

questions.question: Which algorithm is common in time-sharing and interactive systems?
questions.explanation: Round Robin is common in time-sharing and interactive systems.

questions.question: The PCB lets the OS:

options.B: Keep track of a process even when it is not executing

questions.explanation: The PCB lets the OS keep track of a process even when it is not executing.

questions.question: The analogy used for shared memory is:

options.C: Many users working on one shared online document

questions.explanation: Shared memory is compared to many users working on one shared online document.

questions.question: The analogy used for message passing is:
questions.explanation: Message passing is compared to a group chat.

questions.question: In the ATM example, IPC is needed because:

options.D: Separate processes for card/PIN, account verification and withdrawal must exchange information and coordinate

questions.explanation: The separate ATM processes must exchange information and coordinate, so IPC is needed.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true?

options.A: A process in Suspend Blocked is waiting for an event
options.B: A suspended process can execute while outside main memory
options.C: A process in Ready is waiting for the CPU
options.D: A Blocked process waits for an event such as I/O

questions.explanation: A suspended process cannot execute while outside main memory, so the statement is false.
